---
title: "Publication-ready tables and reports"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 110)
library(IRTistic)
set.seed(3)
```

## Tables

`irt_table()` formats any IRTistic result consistently: fixed decimals,
APA-style p-values, SEs in parentheses, readable column names, a caption
and a note.

```{r}
fit <- irt_fit(sim_irt(600, 10, "2pl"), "2pl")
irt_table(fit)
```

In an R Markdown or Quarto document, ask for HTML, Markdown or LaTeX:

```{r}
irt_table(item_fit(fit), format = "html")
```

```{r}
irt_table(reliability(fit), format = "html")
irt_table(classification_accuracy(fit, theta_cuts = c(-0.5, 1)), format = "html")
```

Write straight to a file for Word, Excel or a journal template:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
irt_table(fit, file = "table2-item-parameters.csv")
irt_table(sx2(fit), file = "table3-sx2.html")
```

## Plots

Every `plot_*()` function returns a ggplot, so ordinary ggplot2 code
customises it:

```{r}
plot_icc(fit, items = 1:4) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~item, ncol = 4) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Item characteristic curves for the anxiety scale")
```

Save a figure at journal resolution with `ggplot2::ggsave()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ggplot2::ggsave("figure1-wright-map.png", plot_wright(fit), width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

## One-call reports

`irt_report()` writes a self-contained HTML report with every table and
figure for a model: overview, parameters, reliability, item fit, S-X²,
local dependence, dimensionality, Wright map, curves, a score table and,
optionally, DIF. Many-facet models get a FACETS-style report.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
irt_report(fit, "my-analysis.html", author = "Your Name", group = my_groups)
```
